title.en: Detachment, Absorption & Everyday Recall
title.zh: 距离感、投入与日常回忆

seoTitle.en: Detachment & Everyday Recall Reflection: Four Experience Topics
seoTitle.zh: 距离感与日常回忆反思：四个体验主题

description.en: Twenty original descriptions of self-experience, surroundings, absorption and uncertainty in everyday recall. Keep private category records and read four complete free guides, without a dissociation score, identity claim or diagnosis.
description.zh: 20条原创描述，回顾自身体验、环境、投入及日常回忆不确定。保留私人类别记录，阅读四篇完整免费指南，不生成解离分数、身份主张或诊断。

introduction.en: Adults can recall their own ordinary experiences over the past four weeks without deciding what caused them. A felt distance, an absorbing activity and uncertainty in recall are different descriptions. No traumatic history, personal narrative or evidence of an event is requested.
introduction.zh: 成年人可以回顾过去四周自身普通体验，无需先决定原因。距离感、投入活动与回忆不确定是不同描述，不要求创伤史、私人叙述或事件证据。

instructions.en: Use recollection only, with an unscored option for no opportunity, unclear recall or withholding. No body or reality checks, recreated sensations, document search, memory reconstruction or contact with another person is needed. Every full guide and the same support information remain public.
instructions.zh: 只用回忆作答；无机会、回忆不清或保留回答可选未计分。无需身体或现实检查、重做感受、查文件、重建记忆或联系别人。全部全文与相同支持说明始终公开。

title.en: Experience of self — Complete Experience Guide
title.zh: 自身体验：完整体验指南

headline.en: Experience of self — Complete Experience Guide
headline.zh: 自身体验：完整体验指南

summary.en: These descriptions concern feeling like an observer, an unfamiliar voice, an automatic-feeling action, distance from a named emotion and less connection with bodily sensations. They record how a moment felt. They do not state that you left your body, became another person or lacked a real self.
summary.zh: 这些描述涉及旁观感、声音陌生、动作自动感、与能说出的情绪有距离，以及与身体感受联系变弱。它们记录片刻怎样被体验，不认定离开身体、变成另一个人或缺少真实自我。

scoreReading.en: Five descriptions retain six category counts without a clinical score, identity inference or causal conclusion.
scoreReading.zh: 五条描述保留六类计数，不生成临床分数、身份推断或原因结论。

title.en: Experience of self — Complete Experience Guide
title.zh: 自身体验：完整体验指南

description.en: These descriptions concern feeling like an observer, an unfamiliar voice, an automatic-feeling action, distance from a named emotion and less connection with bodily sensations. They record how a moment felt. They do not state that you left your body, became another person or lacked a real self.
description.zh: 这些描述涉及旁观感、声音陌生、动作自动感、与能说出的情绪有距离，以及与身体感受联系变弱。它们记录片刻怎样被体验，不认定离开身体、变成另一个人或缺少真实自我。

title.en: A felt distance is not an identity finding
title.zh: 感到距离，不是身份发现

paragraphs.en: These descriptions concern feeling like an observer, an unfamiliar voice, an automatic-feeling action, distance from a named emotion and less connection with bodily sensations. They record how a moment felt. They do not state that you left your body, became another person or lacked a real self.
paragraphs.zh: 这些描述涉及旁观感、声音陌生、动作自动感、与能说出的情绪有距离，以及与身体感受联系变弱。它们记录片刻怎样被体验，不认定离开身体、变成另一个人或缺少真实自我。

paragraphs.en: A description of felt distance cannot identify depersonalisation, dissociative identity disorder or a cause. It is also different from rating the strength of an emotion. You do not need to inspect a mirror, listen repeatedly to your voice or check your body to decide whether the prompt happened.
paragraphs.zh: 距离感描述不能识别人格解体、分离性身份障碍或原因，也不同于评价情绪强度。无需检查镜子、反复听自己的声音或检查身体来判断题述是否发生。

title.en: Five descriptions, six labels
title.zh: 五条描述，六类标签

paragraphs.en: Six category counts add to five selected descriptions. They do not count incidents, minutes, symptoms or a percentage of your life. IDs are not points. There is no total, mean, highest topic, cutoff, diagnosis or risk category.
paragraphs.zh: 六类计数合计五条所选描述，不数事件、分钟、症状或生活比例。标识不是点数，没有总分、均分、最高主题、切点、诊断或风险类别。

paragraphs.en: One often, one sometimes and three unscored remain those five choices. No opportunity, unclear recall and withholding stay distinct from did not notice on relevant occasions. A fully unscored topic gives no finding. Few labels cannot exclude a concern, and frequent labels cannot establish a disorder or its cause.
paragraphs.zh: 一条较常、一条有时、三条未计分，就保持五个选择。无机会、回忆不清与保留回答，不变成有机会时没有注意到。全未计分不提供发现；少量不排除担忧，频繁选择也不能确定疾病或原因。

title.en: A fictional example with limits
title.zh: 一个有边界的虚构例子

paragraphs.en: Imagine a fictional adult recalling a routine conversation in which their own voice felt unfamiliar. They still know that they were speaking. The record can retain that experience without explaining its cause or turning it into an identity claim. If they cannot recall a relevant moment, it can stay unscored.
paragraphs.zh: 设想一位虚构成年人回忆一次普通谈话，当时自己的声音显得陌生，但仍知道自己正在说话。记录可以保留体验，不解释原因，也不转成身份主张。想不起相关片刻时，可保持未计分。

paragraphs.en: The example is not an expected answer, evidence about you or a task to repeat. A later difference can reflect opportunity, interpretation or recollection. It cannot establish recovery, deterioration, memory recovery or treatment response.
paragraphs.zh: 例子不是期待答案、关于你的证据或要重复的任务。后来差异可反映机会、理解或回忆，不能确定恢复、恶化、记忆找回或治疗反应。

title.en: Original descriptions with a bounded purpose
title.zh: 有边界的原创描述

paragraphs.en: These twenty bilingual descriptions and four overlapping editorial topics are original and unvalidated. They are not the Dissociative Experiences Scale, DES-II or a screening instrument for dissociative identity disorder. The four-week window is editorial, with no norms, clinical thresholds or established language equivalence.
paragraphs.zh: 20条双语描述与四个可重叠编辑主题均为未经验证的原创，不是解离体验量表、DES-II或分离性身份障碍筛查工具。四周范围是编辑选择，没有常模、临床界值或已建立的语言等值。

paragraphs.en: Related feelings, attention and trauma-response pages keep their own questions and methods. An overlapping word does not make their scores interchangeable or explain this record. Nothing here verifies a trauma history, hidden identity, external reality or a neurological or psychiatric cause.
paragraphs.zh: 相关感受、注意与提醒反应页面保留自身问题和方法。词语重叠不使分数可互换，也不解释本记录。这里不核实创伤史、隐藏身份、外部现实或神经与精神原因。

title.en: An optional way to describe the concern
title.zh: 一种可选的担忧表达方式

paragraphs.en: If you want a private note, you can distinguish the ordinary activity, the felt distance and whether you wanted support. No detailed personal history is needed. Do not repeat an uncomfortable sensation or use a count to decide whether your experience is real or deserves attention.
paragraphs.zh: 若愿意私下记录，可以区分普通活动、感到的距离及是否希望获得支持。无需详细私人历史，也不要重复不舒服感觉，或用计数判断体验是否真实、是否值得关注。

paragraphs.en: You can leave any suggestion aside and read without doing an exercise. No result requires a changed behaviour, disclosure of private details or proof that you can control an experience. A practical need deserves attention on its own terms, without a questionnaire threshold.
paragraphs.zh: 可不采用任何建议，也可只读、不练习。结果不要求改变行为、披露私人细节或证明能控制体验。实际需要可以按自身情况被认真对待，无需问卷门槛。

title.en: Support, stopping and privacy
title.zh: 支持、停止与隐私

paragraphs.en: If experiences are new, distressing or affecting everyday life, you can discuss them with a qualified healthcare professional without completing this page or reaching a count. The page cannot assess causes, medical need or urgency. Do not delay care or change treatment because of a record. If immediate danger is present or you cannot stay safe, seek appropriate local emergency assistance rather than continuing.
paragraphs.zh: 体验若是新出现、令人困扰或影响日常，可以向合格医疗专业人士讨论，无需完成或达到计数。页面不评原因、医疗需要或紧急程度；不要因记录推迟照护或改变治疗。有即时危险或无法保障安全时，寻求当地合适的紧急援助而非继续。

paragraphs.en: All full guides and support information remain public for every answer pattern. Answers stay in current-page memory, without drafts, submission, questionnaire analytics or a private result address. Exit, refresh, leaving and retake clear them. Copying includes only the public title and entry, without selections, counts or a personal history.
paragraphs.zh: 全部全文与支持说明对任何组合都公开。回答只在当前页面内存，不存草稿、不提交、不作问卷分析、没有私人结果地址。退出、刷新、离页与重做会清除；复制只含公开标题与入口，不含选择、计数或私人历史。

title.en: Support, stopping and privacy

paragraphs.en: If experiences are new, distressing or affecting everyday life, you can discuss them with a qualified healthcare professional without completing this page or reaching a count. The page cannot assess causes, medical need or urgency. Do not delay care or change treatment because of a record. If immediate danger is present or you cannot stay safe, seek appropriate local emergency assistance rather than continuing.

paragraphs.en: All full guides and support information remain public for every answer pattern. Answers stay in current-page memory, without drafts, submission, questionnaire analytics or a private result address. Exit, refresh, leaving and retake clear them. Copying includes only the public title and entry, without selections, counts or a personal history.

summary.en: This topic concerns attention narrowing during a chosen activity, losing track of elapsed time, daydreaming, noticing mind-wandering and continuing a familiar action while thinking about something else. These are descriptions of attention. They do not establish missing memories, impaired functioning or a clinical dissociative state.

title.en: Being absorbed is not automatically a disorder
title.zh: 投入其中，不自动等于疾病

paragraphs.en: An engaging activity can be welcome, while an interruption of a task can feel unwelcome. paragraphs.zh: 投入活动可能合意，任务被打断也可能不合意。记录不为两者指定理想分数，也不以注意返回抵扣其他描述。它不识别ADHD、心流、创造力或非凡专注能力。

title.zh: 五条描述，六类标签

paragraphs.en: Six category counts add to five selected descriptions. They do not count incidents, minutes, symptoms or a percentage of your life. IDs are not points. There is no total, mean, highest topic, cutoff, diagnosis or risk category.
paragraphs.zh: 六类计数合计五条所选描述，不数事件、分钟、症状或生活比例。标识不是点数，没有总分、均分、最高主题、切点、诊断或风险类别。

paragraphs.en: One often, one sometimes and three unscored remain those five choices. No opportunity, unclear recall and withholding stay distinct from did not notice on relevant occasions. A fully unscored topic gives no finding. Few labels cannot exclude a concern, and frequent labels cannot establish a disorder or its cause.
paragraphs.zh: 一条较常、一条有时、三条未计分，就保持五个选择。无机会、回忆不清与保留回答，不变成有机会时没有注意到。全未计分不提供发现；少量不排除担忧，频繁选择也不能确定疾病或原因。

title.en: A fictional example with limits
title.zh: 一个有边界的虚构例子

paragraphs.en: Imagine a fictional reader noticing that more time has passed than expected while following a story. They then return attention to the room. Both observations can remain without calling the first a lost memory or the second proof that no concern exists. The example is not a task to recreate.
paragraphs.zh: 设想一位虚构读者跟随故事时，发现过去的时间比预想多，随后把注意转回房间。两者都可保留，不把前者叫记忆缺失，也不把后者当成没有担忧的证明。例子不是要重做的任务。

paragraphs.en: The example is not an expected answer, evidence about you or a task to repeat. A later difference can reflect opportunity, interpretation or recollection. It cannot establish recovery, deterioration, memory recovery or treatment response.
paragraphs.zh: 例子不是期待答案、关于你的证据或要重复的任务。后来差异可反映机会、理解或回忆，不能确定恢复、恶化、记忆找回或治疗反应。

paragraphs.en: These twenty bilingual descriptions and four overlapping editorial topics are original and unvalidated. They are not the Dissociative Experiences Scale, DES-II or a screening instrument for dissociative identity disorder. The four-week window is editorial, with no norms, clinical thresholds or established language equivalence.

paragraphs.zh: 若私下反思有用，可以区分什么吸引注意、原本还想做什么及后来注意到什么。无需制造干扰或强迫长时间投入。实际担忧应按具体情境考虑，不靠计数决定。

title.zh: 四个体验主题，不设临床分数

question.en: Does this diagnose dissociation or identity disorders?
question.zh: 会诊断解离或身份障碍吗？

answer.en: No. It records descriptions without a clinical score, screening threshold, identity inference or diagnosis. It cannot explain a memory gap or verify an event. Professional assessment uses other information.
answer.zh: 不会。它记录描述，不设临床分数、筛查门槛、身份推断或诊断，不能解释记忆缺口或核实事件。专业评估需要其他信息。

question.en: Should I recreate an experience or recover a memory?
question.zh: 需要重做体验或找回记忆吗？

answer.en: No. Use only what you already recall, leave uncertainty unscored and stop if you want. No check, reconstruction or personal evidence is needed to read all guides or ask for support.
answer.zh: 不需要。只用已有回忆，不确定可保持未计分，也可随时停止。阅读全文或求助无需检查、重建或私人证据。
